subject: Human Rights Commission Recruitment and Outreach
overview: The Medford Human Rights Commission met to welcome new members, plan recruitment strategies for three vacant seats, and discuss upcoming community events. The commission also adopted a new official letterhead and established meeting conduct guidelines to foster respectful dialogue.

items.title: Roll Call and Introductions
items.summary: Commissioners and staff introduced themselves and welcomed new members to the body.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the June 2023 meeting notes as official minutes.

items.title: Outreach and Recruitment Strategy
items.summary: Members discussed attending local festivals to distribute recruitment cards and socialize with residents to fill vacant seats.

items.title: International Human Rights Day Planning
items.summary: The commission explored drafting a joint statement or seeking a mayoral proclamation to commemorate the day on December 10.

items.title: Recruitment and Youth Participation
items.summary: Director Nwajei provided an update on investigating age requirements for membership and reaching out to middle and high school students.

items.title: Official Letterhead Adoption
items.summary: The commission approved a new standardized letterhead design for formal correspondence and reports to the City Council.

items.title: Discrimination Incident Report
items.summary: Director Nwajei informed the commission of an alleged incident of discrimination at a local business and confirmed that a police report had been filed.

items.title: Commission Touchstones and Public Participation
items.summary: Members reviewed draft conduct guidelines and discussed implementing time limits for public comments to maintain meeting order.

items.title: Announcements and Public Comment
items.summary: The commission heard updates regarding the Disability Resource Fair and the Charter Study Committee survey before receiving a volunteer offer for note-taking.
